| Scene description | • S09-A is a commercial pedestrian food street in Liangdao Street, Wuchang District, with stainless-steel sorting bins beside shops and catering stalls, signs, and pedestrians.<br>• S09-A-02: a clean open-lidded bin does not overflow or visibly spill.<br>• S09-A-05: a partly transparent printed bag containing some residue accumulates at the curb–asphalt boundary amid rain marks, near a yellow shared bicycle and pole. Other supplied images had no detected targets, with no overflow or accumulation observed. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should be conveniently located without obstructing pedestrians, clean, and free of spillage or accumulation. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 21.<br>• Casual dumping, scattering, or stockpiling in public areas is prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 28.<br>• Bin surroundings require prompt cleaning and collection without retained waste. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 15.<br>• Commercial and catering areas require increased collection frequency against overflow and accumulation. Standard for the Provision of Urban Environmental Sanitation Facilities (CJJ 27-2012), Section 5.2.3.<br>• Failure to clean or collection omissions impairing appearance may entail correction orders and fines. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two accumulations near busy food stalls create sanitation risks and visual pollution, impairing appearance without bin overflow. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: the S09-A-05 bag locally pollutes ground and risks odors and insects. Possible short-term impacts: breezes in cloudy weather may spread waste; rain may create contaminated runoff affecting pavement, pedestrians, and urban appearance. |
| Potential causes | - Delayed collection may leave disposal unaddressed and encourage bags outside bins.<br>- Individuals or vendors may place bags casually at the curb.<br>- The printed bag beside S09-A-05, shared bicycles, and a pole suggest frequent pedestrian or vendor activity and possible catering packaging.<br>- Verify collection records, overflow alerts, and business disposal observations to distinguish delays from littering. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, routine accumulation may cause vectors and odors, impair health and street quality, undermine perceptions of management efficiency, and reduce commercial attractiveness. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** clear reported accumulations at S09-A-02 and S09-A-05, wash and disinfect bin surroundings, and increase responsible organizations' inspections and collections.<br>- **Long-term measures:** add temporary bins or mobile points, optimize routes and schedules, educate businesses and users, and link location reports, collection response, and feedback. |
| Priority | **Medium.** Accumulations on a busy commercial street pose sanitation and appearance risks without a public safety emergency. Complete removal and rectification within 24 hours. |
